implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: keep the two halves the pattern describes separate - a recipient computation that turns a message into an ordered set of recipient identifiers (from configuration, headers or a registry), and a traversal that clones the message once per entry and delivers the copy to that recipient's channel. Let the traversal, not the recipient computation, own error handling: define a per-recipient policy (fail-fast or continue), a send timeout, and a record of what actually went out. Validate computed recipient values against an allow-list before they can steer traffic, bound the number of recipients and the parallelism, and make receivers idempotent because partial retries are normal.
code_sketch:
recipients = resolve(message)          # registry / config / header -> ordered set
for r in recipients:
    copy = message.clone()             # the pattern forwards a copy, not a shared object
    deliver(r, copy)                   # per-recipient policy: timeout, retry, record
# continue-with-remaining vs abort is a deliberate policy, not an accident
pitfalls: Letting the recipient computation mutate the message, so recipients later in the same fan-out see different content.
No per-recipient timeout or failure policy: one stuck destination stalls the whole list.
Treating the recipient set as trusted input even though it frequently arrives with the message.

Wrong move: use Recipient List where a publish-subscribe channel owns membership -> the router duplicates subscription state and can miss consumers -> instead let the broker or Publish-Subscribe Channel maintain subscriptions.

Wrong move: accept endpoint URIs directly from an untrusted message header -> a producer can route data to unauthorized destinations -> instead map trusted recipient IDs through an allow-listed registry before dispatch.

Wrong move: assume one fan-out is atomic -> one failed send leaves partial delivery and unsafe retries -> instead record per-recipient outcomes, bound timeouts and concurrency, and require idempotent receivers.
